title: A complete curve with a nontrivial connected linear-group action is a projective line
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All groups are affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and all subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Let $H$ be smooth and connected [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Let $C$ be a smooth proper integral finite-type $F$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-pc-integral-scheme] of Krull dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $a:H\times_F C\to C$ be an $F$-morphism satisfying the action unit and multiplication identities. If $a$ is not the second projection, then $C$ is $F$-isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1_F=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};\operatorname{Spec}F)$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. There is no characteristic restriction.

proof.text: Put $T=H\times_F C$. It is smooth over $F$ by smooth base change and composition [lem-sfb-stack-smooth-permanence], hence reduced by [lem-sfb-space-smooth-reduced-locality], applied over the reduced scheme $\operatorname{Spec}F$. It is finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. Its closed points are dense by [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space], and are $F$-rational by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base]. Let $W$ be the disjoint union of their copies of $\operatorname{Spec}F$, mapping to $T$. If $a(h,x)=x$ for all $h\in H(F),x\in C(F)$, the two maps $a,\operatorname{pr}_2:T\to C$ agree after $W\to T$: rational points of a fibre product are pairs by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Since $C/F$ is separated by properness [def-weil-proper-morphism], the dense-image extensionality [lem-sfb-relative-separated-dominant-ext] makes these maps equal, a contradiction. Thus choose $h,x$ with $hx\ne x$.

source.place: Proposition 20.5 and 20.2--20.3, printed p.408; coordinate version of the solvable reduction using Proposition 16.55(c) and Corollary 16.56, printed p.344.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-borel-conjugation-cover], choose a Borel subgroup $B\subseteq H$ and $g\in H(F), b\in B(F)$ with $h=gbg^{-1}$. Put $y=g^{-1}x$. If $by=y$, the action identities give $hx=gby=gy=x$, contradiction. Hence the restricted action of the smooth connected solvable group $B$ moves $y$ by $b$.

source.place: Proposition 20.5 and 20.2--20.3, printed p.408; coordinate version of the solvable reduction using Proposition 16.55(c) and Corollary 16.56, printed p.344.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-split-solvable-torsors-and-variety] to $B$: it is split solvable and there is an $F$-scheme isomorphism $\theta:\mathbf A_F^r\times_F(\mathbf G_m)^s\simeq B$. Write $p=\theta^{-1}(1)$ and $q=\theta^{-1}(b)$. In the product of $r+s$ coordinates, form $p_0=p, p_1,\ldots,p_{r+s}=q$ by changing one coordinate at a time from its $p$-value to its $q$-value. The values of $z\mapsto\theta(z)y$ at the two ends are $y$ and $by\ne y$, so some consecutive values differ. Fix all other coordinates at their values in these consecutive points and vary that coordinate. This defines an $F$-morphism from $Q=\mathbf G_a$ (an affine coordinate) or $Q=\mathbf G_m$ (a torus coordinate) to the product, hence a morphism $u:Q\to C$. The coordinate maps are substitution homomorphisms of polynomial or Laurent polynomial rings [def-sc-gm-ga, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Two $F$-points have different images under $u$, so $u$ cannot factor through an $F$-point. The case $r+s=0$ is excluded by the unequal endpoint values.

source.place: Proposition 20.5 and 20.2--20.3, printed p.408; coordinate version of the solvable reduction using Proposition 16.55(c) and Corollary 16.56, printed p.344.

proof.text: The coordinate ring of $Q$ is $F[t]$ or $F[t,t^{-1}]$ [def-sc-gm-ga]. Both are domains: the highest nonzero coefficient of a product of nonzero polynomials is the product of their highest coefficients, and multiplying Laurent polynomials by powers of $t$ reduces to that case. Both have fraction field $F(t)$ [def-weil-rational-function-field]: in the Laurent case the extra generator $t^{-1}$ is already in that field, and every Laurent fraction is a fraction of polynomials after multiplying numerator and denominator by powers of $t$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field], $Q$ is integral and $F(Q)\simeq F(t)$ as $F$-algebras.

source.place: Proposition 20.5 and 20.2--20.3, printed p.408; coordinate version of the solvable reduction using Proposition 16.55(c) and Corollary 16.56, printed p.344.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-curve-nonconstant-generic-criterion] to the integral source $Q$ and the smooth integral dimension-one target $C$. Nonconstancy from step 3 gives an injective $F$-homomorphism $u^*:F(C)\hookrightarrow F(Q)\simeq F(t)$. Let $E$ be its image, an intermediate field. By [lem-sfb-curve-function-field-arithmetic], $\operatorname{trdeg}_F F(C)=\dim C=1$. Thus $E$ is strictly larger than $F$: if the image contained only constants, the injective $F$-map would identify $F(C)$ with $F$, whose transcendence degree is zero. The map $F(C)\to E$ is an $F$-isomorphism by its definition as the image.

source.place: Proposition 20.5 and 20.2--20.3, printed p.408; coordinate version of the solvable reduction using Proposition 16.55(c) and Corollary 16.56, printed p.344.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-luroth-rational-intermediate-field] applied to $E\subseteq F(t)$, there is an $F$-isomorphism $F(t)\simeq E$. Composing it with the inverse of $F(C)\simeq E$ from step 5 yields an $F$-isomorphism $F(t)\simeq F(C)$. No separability of $u$ is asserted or needed.

source.place: Proposition 20.5 and 20.2--20.3, printed p.408; coordinate version of the solvable reduction using Proposition 16.55(c) and Corollary 16.56, printed p.344.

proof.text: Let $P=\mathbf P^1_F$ with the exact projective-space model in the statement. By [lem-asd-projective-line-genus-zero], $P$ is a smooth proper connected curve of dimension one. By the integral clause of [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings], it is integral. The standard-chart statement [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts], with index set $\{0,1\}$ and base $\operatorname{Spec}F$, gives a nonempty affine open $U\subseteq P$ with coordinate ring $F[t]$. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], the generic-stalk field $F(P)$ is its fraction field, hence $F(P)\simeq F(t)$ by [def-weil-rational-function-field]. Together with step 6 this gives an $F$-isomorphism $\alpha:F(P)\simeq F(C)$.

source.place: Proposition 20.5 and 20.2--20.3, printed p.408; coordinate version of the solvable reduction using Proposition 16.55(c) and Corollary 16.56, printed p.344.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-proper-curve-function-field-morphisms] to $C$ and $P$, both smooth proper integral dimension-one curves: $\alpha$ gives $f:C\to P$, and $\alpha^{-1}$ gives $g:P\to C$. Its identity and composition clauses give $(g\circ f)^*=\alpha\circ\alpha^{-1}=\operatorname{id}_{F(C)}$ and $(f\circ g)^*=\alpha^{-1}\circ\alpha=\operatorname{id}_{F(P)}$. Its injectivity then gives $g\circ f=\operatorname{id}_C$ and $f\circ g=\operatorname{id}_P$. Thus $f$ is the required $F$-isomorphism.
